terms.meaning: A scatter plot where the size of each dot shows a third number.
How far a project ran past its planned time.
A project's step in its life, such as planning, under construction, or operating.
The chart drawing library this file imports.

used_by: pages/Analysis.tsx (named in a comment, path not confirmed)

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and shared vocabulary note
sections.what: Brings in the React library, a saved-settings hook, shared colours and the chart library parts. Nothing is shown to the user from this part.
sections.why: Likely reason: the saved-settings hook keeps some chart choices after a page reload, based on its name. This is not confirmed in the reviewed part.

sections.name: LIFECYCLE_ORDER
sections.title: Order of project stages
sections.what: Lists the project stages in order, from early planning through construction and operation to on hold and cancelled.
sections.why: The comment says the Analysis page uses this same list for its timeline view and filter order.
sections.watch_out: A stage missing from this list has no set position in the ordering.

sections.name: STAGE_COLOR
sections.title: Colour for each stage
sections.what: Gives each stage a colour, so stages can be told apart on the chart. On-hold projects get amber, and cancelled projects get a dark grey.
sections.why: Likely reason: colour helps a reader spot the stage of each project at a glance.
sections.watch_out: Operating and Operational share the same colour, so the chart cannot tell them apart by colour.

sections.name: stageColor
sections.title: Looking up a stage colour
sections.what: Returns the colour for a stage name. Any name not in the colour table gets a standard grey instead.
sections.why: Likely reason: a new or unexpected stage still draws in grey rather than breaking the chart.
sections.watch_out: The name must match exactly, including capitals and underscores, or the stage silently shows grey.

sections.name: topQuartileAvg
sections.title: Average of the worst quarter
sections.what: Takes a list of numbers and returns the average of its highest quarter, or nothing if the list is empty. The chart uses it to place the dashed red benchmark lines for cost and schedule.
sections.why: Likely reason: the benchmark lines show how the worst projects typically perform, so one average of the top quarter is drawn.
sections.watch_out: The function treats higher numbers as worse, which is correct for cost and schedule overruns but would be wrong for any measure where higher is better.

sections.name: BubblePoint
sections.title: Shape of a plotted project
sections.what: Defines the information each project needs to appear as a bubble: name, phase, country, technology, contractor, cost and schedule figures, bubble size, capacity, and any note about an estimated delay.
sections.why: The comments say this shape was moved from the Analysis page and that new data sources must produce the same shape.
sections.watch_out: Renaming or removing a field here breaks the page that builds these points and any new data adapter.

sections.name: BubbleChartConfig, SizeMode, EMPTY_CHART_FILTERS
sections.title: Chart mode settings
sections.what: Lists the settings the parent passes in: whether the horizontal axis is in years or percent, and whether bubble size is equal, based on capex, or based on capacity.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the comments. The chart reads these settings instead of holding them itself.
sections.watch_out: Only the three listed size modes are valid, so a new size option must be added here and in the chart logic together.

sections.name: isChartFilters, FilterKey, FILTER_LABELS
sections.title: Checking saved filter settings
sections.what: Checks that filter choices read back from browser storage have the expected shape. Also defines the four filter categories and the labels shown for them.
sections.why: Likely reason: saved data can be old or damaged, and this check stops bad data from crashing the chart.
sections.watch_out: A new filter category must be added to the check, the type, and the labels together, or saved choices for it will be discarded.

sections.name: applySize
sections.title: Working out bubble sizes
sections.what: Computes each project's bubble size from the chosen mode. Equal mode gives all bubbles the same size. Capex mode uses the budget. Capacity mode uses only the most common capacity unit, and projects in other units get no size.
sections.why: The comments say bubble area should match the value and that different units must not be compared.
sections.watch_out: If most projects use an unexpected unit, many capacity bubbles disappear without any error message.

sections.name: CostScheduleBubbleChartProps
sections.title: Inputs the chart accepts
sections.what: Lists everything the parent passes in: the projects, the chosen settings, the selected set, click handlers, and optional filter and saving options.
sections.why: The comments say selection is owned by the caller, so the chart only shows selections and reports clicks.
sections.watch_out: The chart does not remember selections on its own, so a parent that does not update the selected set will show no change when a bubble is clicked.

sections.name: FilterMenu
sections.title: Filter dropdown with checkboxes
sections.what: A button that opens a list of checkboxes for one filter category. The button shows how many boxes are ticked.
sections.why: Lets readers narrow the chart to chosen technologies, companies, countries, or phases.
sections.watch_out: Underscores in option names are shown as spaces, so two options that differ only by an underscore would look the same.

sections.name: BubbleTooltip
sections.title: Hover box for a project
sections.what: The box that appears when a reader points at a bubble. It shows the project name, cost overrun percent, schedule deviation (with an approximate tag and note when the delay is estimated), capacity, capex, phase, and country.
sections.why: Gives the details of each project without leaving the chart.
sections.watch_out: Capex is divided by 1000 and labelled billions, which assumes the stored budget is in millions.

sections.name: CostScheduleBubbleChart (part 1)
sections.title: Setting up data, filters and controls
sections.what: Keeps the filter selections, works out which filter choices exist, keeps only projects that match the filters, and builds the size and filter controls above the chart.
sections.why: Likely reason: filters apply to the whole chart, and the saved-setting name depends on the tool and industry so each one remembers its own choices.
sections.watch_out: Filters are saved in browser storage only when a persist key is given. Without it they reset on page reload.

sections.name: CostScheduleBubbleChart (part 2)
sections.title: Recovering from zero-width charts and preparing series
sections.what: Watches the chart container. If it first appears with zero width, it forces one clean redraw once a real width arrives. It also computes the benchmark lines, groups projects by phase in lifecycle order, sets the size range, and collects projects with no size.
sections.why: The comment says the chart can paint blank after a zero-size first draw during page reloads or route changes.
sections.watch_out: Removing the redraw logic may bring back blank charts after navigation, and the bug is hard to see in tests.

sections.name: CostScheduleBubbleChart (part 3)
sections.title: Hollow marker for missing size and empty state
sections.what: Draws a dashed hollow circle for projects that have no usable size, outlined by phase or highlighted when selected. If no project has the needed data, it shows a message instead of a chart.
sections.why: Likely reason: a distinct symbol keeps missing capacity from looking like a real size.
sections.watch_out: The hollow marker has a fixed size on purpose, so it never reflects a value.

sections.name: CostScheduleBubbleChart (part 4)
sections.title: Axes, benchmark lines and phase series start
sections.what: Sets up the two axes, the size scale, the hover box, and the dashed red benchmark lines. Then starts one set of dots per phase when selection mode is off, where clicking opens the project.
sections.why: The comment records a verified recharts 2.15.4 issue: wrapping the per-phase series in a fragment makes the whole plot blank with no error, so flat arrays are used instead.
sections.watch_out: Wrapping these series in a React fragment silently blanks the whole chart.

sections.name: CostScheduleBubbleChart (part 5)
sections.title: Selected and unselected bubbles
sections.what: In selection mode, splits each phase into selected dots (blue outline) and unselected dots (faded), and makes clicks toggle selection. Also draws the hollow no-size markers and starts the legend.
sections.why: Gives clear feedback on what has been picked for the benchmark.
sections.watch_out: The same click toggles selection in selection mode but opens the project page in normal mode, which can surprise readers.

sections.name: CostScheduleBubbleChart (part 6)
sections.title: Legend and size footnote
sections.what: Shows the phase legend with counts, a key for hollow markers with their count, and a footnote explaining what bubble size means and what the dashed red lines show.
sections.why: Explains the chart so readers can read it without help.
sections.watch_out: The hollow-marker label changes with the size mode, so a new size option needs its own label here.

summary: Part of the benchmark cost-versus-schedule bubble chart. The reviewed part defines the project stage order and a colour for each stage. The chart itself lives in sections that were not reviewed here.
purpose: Plots benchmark projects by how far their cost and schedule ran over, with dot sizes and filters. The outline lists a filter menu, a hover tooltip and size options, but those parts were not read.
why: The top comment says the stage names and colours were moved here from the Analysis page, so that page and this chart share one definition.
how: In the reviewed part: stage names are listed in order from planning to cancelled, each stage gets a colour, and a helper returns that colour with grey as the fallback. The remaining steps could not be verified from the sections given.
inputs: A stage name as text, such as UNDER_CONSTRUCTION. Other inputs, such as project data, filters and size choices, are not visible in the reviewed part.
outputs: A colour code for a stage, and the stage order list that other screens use. Chart output was not reviewed.
risks: Stage names must match exactly, and anything else gets grey. Two stages share one colour, so they look the same on the chart.
debug: If a stage shows grey, compare its name with the keys in the stage colour table. If stages appear in the wrong order, check the stage order list. For chart problems, the rest of the file must be read, and this note does not cover them.
